01 / About us

We started with a small act of kindness.

Via Victoria was founded in the run-up to Christmas 2025, inspired by a simple idea: to help where it can make a tangible difference.

One of our first initiatives was preparing St Nicholas gift packages for children. It was a small gesture, but it showed us how even simple acts of kindness can bring joy and help us find our direction. We hope to continue this tradition this year.

Our team is small. We handle much of the work ourselves — the website, projects, administration, accounting, and communication with institutions and businesses. We are learning as we go, and Via Victoria is evolving with us.

We are not a large organisation with an extensive infrastructure. We are people who believe that even small, well-directed support can make a real difference.

As we grow, we want to keep our focus on practical help: supporting people wherever we can, sharing experience and connecting those who want to help with those who need it.

What we do →
02 / Our experience

Sharing what we have learned.

During difficult times, the information we needed was not always easy to find in one place. We want to share the experiences and topics that may also help others.

Leukaemia, explained simply

A subject we know from personal experience. Here you can explore straightforward explanations of terms we encountered as parents.

This is not the main focus of Via Victoria. It is one part of our experience. We created the series around questions and medical terms we worked to understand ourselves, so we could explain them to our family in simple language.

What this series is — and what it is not.

This series is not medical guidance or treatment advice. It offers a simple overview of some of the experiences our family has been through and the terms we encountered during treatment.

Leukaemia and its treatment are far more complex than a few illustrations can explain. That is why diagnosis and treatment must always be guided by qualified medical professionals. We do not aim to teach medicine, only to make some common terms easier to understand. Decisions about an individual diagnosis or treatment always belong to the treating medical team.

The illustrated slides are currently in Slovak. Each episode has an English summary; the original illustrations are preserved.

03 / What we do

Support should be practical.

We want to go beyond big promises and focus on where we can make a meaningful difference in people’s lives.

Supporting families

Practical support tailored to each family’s circumstances and needs.

Support does not always look the same. Sometimes it is a useful item; other times it is a contact, information or help with a problem a family is facing.

Sharing experience

We want to share what we have learned, in a way that is easier for others to understand.

We do not aim to replace professionals. We share practical experience, contacts and clear explanations that may save others time, uncertainty or unnecessary searching.

Our projects

Initiatives built around a real need and a clear purpose.

As we develop, we will present Via Victoria projects here — from small local activities to larger initiatives. For each project, we want to explain what we do and what it achieves.

Addressing wider issues

When a problem affects more than one family.

From experience, we know that families facing difficult circumstances often have to navigate not only illness but also complicated rules, unclear procedures and administrative obstacles. When we identify an issue affecting several people, we try to raise it and look for solutions.

We highlight problemsWhen things do not work as they should.
We engage with institutionsPublic authorities, specialist organisations and other responsible bodies.
We seek solutionsEspecially when one solution could help many families.
04 / How you can help

Every contribution can make a difference.

Here you can find straightforward ways to support Via Victoria.

1–2% of Slovak income tax

A way for eligible Slovak taxpayers to support Via Victoria at no additional cost.

The procedure depends on whether you are an employee, an individual filing a tax return or a company. Our recipient details are provided below. This scheme applies under Slovak tax rules.

NameVia Victoria
Organisation ID (IČO)55476970
Legal formCivic association (Slovakia)
Employee

My employer handles my annual tax settlement

  1. Ask your employer for the official certificate confirming the income tax paid.
  2. Complete the separate Slovak tax-allocation declaration using Via Victoria’s recipient details.
  3. Submit the declaration and employer certificate to the Slovak tax authority by 30 April 2027.
Individual

I file my own tax return

  1. You do not need a separate declaration — enter Via Victoria’s details directly in the relevant section of your Slovak tax return.
  2. This also applies to sole traders and other individuals who file their own tax returns.
  3. The standard filing deadline for the 2026 tax year is 31 March 2027, unless a valid extension applies.
Company / legal entity

The allocation is made through the company tax return

  1. Enter Via Victoria as the recipient and specify the allocated amount in the relevant section of the Slovak corporate tax return.
  2. A company may allocate 2% of its paid income tax if it meets the legal condition of donating at least 0.5% of its paid tax to eligible nonprofit purposes; otherwise the allocation is 1%.
  3. No separate declaration is required.
Download tax-allocation details

Recurring donation

If you would like to contribute regularly, set up a standing order to the same bank account. You decide the amount and frequency.

  • Recipient: Via Victoria
  • IBAN: SK88 1100 0000 0029 4329 7371
  • For example, you might choose €5, €10 or €20 per month, depending on what works for you.
  • You may use “Regular donation” as the payment reference, but this is optional.

Collaboration

For individuals and businesses who would like to offer practical help.

Businesses

Businesses can support us financially or in practical ways — as a one-off contribution, through regular giving or through their own workplace initiative.

  • a corporate donation or ongoing financial support,
  • an employee fundraiser or internal initiative,
  • donating products, materials or services,
  • supporting a particular Via Victoria activity or project.

Individuals

Individuals can contribute too — not only with money, but also with their time, ideas or connections.

  • volunteering when help is needed,
  • sharing information about our activities,
  • supporting a small local initiative,
  • connecting us with people or businesses who may be able to help.

Donating goods

Financial support is not always the only thing needed. A useful item or practical assistance can be just as valuable.

  • gifts and small treats for children or families,
  • hygiene, everyday or leisure items,
  • printing, office supplies or small equipment,
  • other support based on current needs.

Professional expertise

We also value the expertise of individuals and companies who can provide specific professional services.

  • graphic design, websites, photography or video,
  • printing, marketing, public relations or communications,
  • legal, accounting or administrative advice,
  • transport, logistics or other specialised services.

If you can help in any of these ways, please contact us at info@viavictoria.eu.
